review.cortex-xdr.faq.a1: Cortex XDR is Palo Alto Networks' extended detection and response platform that unifies endpoint, network, and cloud data for threat detection. It uses behavioral analytics and machine learning to detect sophisticated attacks across your infrastructure.
review.cortex-xdr.faq.q2: How does Cortex XDR integrate with XSOAR?
review.cortex-xdr.faq.a2: Cortex XSOAR (formerly Demisto) is Palo Alto's security orchestration platform. It integrates with XDR to automate incident response, coordinate actions across security tools, and reduce response times through playbooks and workflows.
review.cortex-xdr.faq.q3: Do I need Palo Alto firewalls to use Cortex XDR?
review.cortex-xdr.faq.a3: No, Cortex XDR works independently and protects endpoints regardless of network infrastructure. However, maximum value comes from integrating with Palo Alto Next-Gen Firewalls and Prisma for unified visibility and policy enforcement.
review.cortex-xdr.faq.q4: How does Cortex XDR compare to traditional EDR?
review.cortex-xdr.faq.a4: Traditional EDR focuses only on endpoints. Cortex XDR extends detection across endpoints, network, and cloud—correlating data from multiple sources to detect attacks that span multiple vectors. This provides better detection of lateral movement and complex attacks.
review.cortex-xdr.faq.q5: What's included in Cortex XDR Pro vs Enterprise?
review.cortex-xdr.faq.a5: Pro includes full EDR/XDR capabilities, behavioral threat protection, and investigation tools. Enterprise adds advanced analytics, host firewall, device control, and deeper XSOAR integration for large-scale operations.
